description: Evaluations to verify that flutter-clean-architecture correctly guides layering decisions, dependency direction, Result pattern usage, and layer responsibilities in any Flutter/Dart project.

evals.expected_output: Identifies at least two violations: (1) Flutter import in domain layer (no Flutter deps allowed in domain), (2) try-catch with UI logic (showDialog) in domain layer — domain should not know about UI, should return Result type instead. The UseCase should return Result<ProductEntity, Exception> and never throw or call UI.

assertions.name: flutter-import-violation-identified
assertions.criteria: Response identifies that 'import package:flutter/material.dart' is a violation — domain layer must not depend on Flutter

assertions.name: ui-in-domain-violation-identified
assertions.criteria: Response identifies that calling showDialog/UI code from domain layer violates Clean Architecture (domain has no knowledge of presentation)

assertions.name: result-pattern-recommended
assertions.criteria: Response recommends returning Result<T, E> or Either<Failure, T> instead of try-catch + throw

assertions.name: correct-return-type-shown
assertions.criteria: Response shows or describes a corrected UseCase signature returning Future<Result<ProductEntity, Exception>> or similar

evals.expected_output: Refactored Cubit using result.fold() or result.when(), with UseCase returning Result<Order, Exception>. The Cubit no longer uses try-catch. The fold has a success branch emitting OrderSuccess and a failure branch emitting OrderError.

assertions.name: try-catch-removed
assertions.criteria: The refactored Cubit code does NOT contain a try-catch block

assertions.name: fold-or-when-used
assertions.criteria: The refactored code uses .fold(), .when(), or pattern matching on the Result type

assertions.name: both-branches-handled
assertions.criteria: Both success and failure branches are handled: success emits OrderSuccess, failure emits OrderError

assertions.name: usecase-return-type-mentioned
assertions.criteria: Response mentions or shows that PlaceOrderUseCase must return Result<Order, Exception> or Either<Failure, Order>

evals.expected_output: The data layer imports and directly calls the presentation layer (CartCubit) — this is a critical violation. Dependencies must flow inward: Presentation → Domain ← Data. Data layer must never import or reference the Presentation layer. The repository should simply return the Result; the Cubit subscribes to the UseCase, not the other way.

assertions.name: data-to-presentation-violation-identified
assertions.criteria: Response clearly identifies the import of CartCubit (presentation) from the Data layer as a dependency direction violation

assertions.name: dependency-rule-explained
assertions.criteria: Response explains the correct direction: Presentation depends on Domain, Data depends on Domain, Domain depends on nobody

assertions.name: fix-described
assertions.criteria: Response describes the fix: remove the CubitCubit import and direct call; repository returns the Result and the Cubit observes it through the UseCase

assertions.name: no-singleton-cubit-endorsed
assertions.criteria: Response does NOT suggest keeping CartCubit.instance pattern as acceptable

evals.expected_output: Separates into ProductModel (Data layer, handles fromJson/toJson, can have rawAttributes) and ProductEntity (Domain layer, pure business fields, Equatable, no JSON methods, no rawAttributes). A Mapper converts Model → Entity. Explains why: entities should not depend on serialization formats, making domain testable without JSON.

assertions.name: separation-recommended
assertions.criteria: Response recommends splitting into a Model (data layer) and an Entity (domain layer)

assertions.name: entity-no-json-methods
assertions.criteria: The recommended Entity does NOT contain fromJson/toJson/rawAttributes — those belong in the Model

assertions.name: mapper-mentioned
assertions.criteria: Response mentions a Mapper class (or mapping function) to convert Model → Entity

assertions.name: equatable-in-entity
assertions.criteria: Response shows or mentions Equatable (or props list) on the Entity for value equality

evals.prompt:
For each of these tasks, tell me which Clean Architecture layer it belongs to and why:
1. Validating that a user's email format is correct before saving
2. Calling the REST API endpoint POST /users
3. Showing a SnackBar when registration succeeds
4. Defining what fields a User has in the system
5. Deciding whether to load data from cache or network
evals.expected_output: 1. Domain (business rule validation in UseCase or Entity). 2. Data (RemoteDataSource calls the API). 3. Presentation (UI reaction in Page/Widget listening to Cubit state). 4. Domain (Entity defines the business object). 5. Data (Repository implementation decides cache vs network strategy).

assertions.name: email-validation-domain
assertions.criteria: Email validation is correctly placed in Domain layer (UseCase or Entity)

assertions.name: api-call-data
assertions.criteria: REST API call is correctly placed in Data layer (DataSource or Repository)

assertions.name: snackbar-presentation
assertions.criteria: Showing a SnackBar is correctly placed in Presentation layer

assertions.name: entity-fields-domain
assertions.criteria: Defining User fields is correctly placed in Domain layer (Entity)

assertions.name: cache-vs-network-data
assertions.criteria: Cache vs network decision is correctly placed in Data layer (Repository implementation)

evals.expected_output: Identifies that CartBloc directly imports GetCurrentUserUseCase from the auth feature — this is a horizontal coupling violation. Features must never import each other directly. The solution is to use AppMediator: when auth feature logs in, it sends UserLoggedInEvent via AppMediator.send(); CartBloc subscribes via AppMediator.on<UserLoggedInEvent>() and reacts without knowing about the auth feature.

assertions.name: direct-feature-import-violation-identified
assertions.criteria: Response identifies that importing GetCurrentUserUseCase from the auth feature inside CartBloc is a cross-feature coupling violation

assertions.name: mediator-solution-proposed
assertions.criteria: Response proposes using AppMediator (or Mediator pattern) as the solution for cross-feature communication

assertions.name: send-and-on-methods-described
assertions.criteria: Response describes or shows AppMediator.send() for publishing events and AppMediator.on<T>() for subscribing

assertions.name: direct-import-not-endorsed
assertions.criteria: Response does NOT suggest keeping the direct import as acceptable or as an alternative

evals.prompt:
I have an existing Flutter app with these issues:
1. BLoC classes use try-catch blocks to handle errors
2. Domain models (User, Product) have fromJson/toJson methods
3. Some BLoC classes call HTTP endpoints directly via Dio
4. There are no repository interfaces — data access is directly in the BLoC

I want to migrate this to Clean Architecture. Where do I start? The app has 8 features and I can't rewrite everything at once.
evals.expected_output: Recommends an incremental, per-feature migration following the 10-step order: start with Failure type and UseCase base interfaces, then extract domain models (remove fromJson), create repository interfaces, move HTTP calls behind DataSources, create RepositoryImpl mapping exceptions to Failure, replace direct calls in BLoC with UseCase calls. Explicitly advises against a full rewrite.

assertions.name: no-full-rewrite-recommended
assertions.criteria: Response explicitly advises against rewriting everything at once and recommends incremental migration

assertions.name: failure-type-or-usecase-base-first
assertions.criteria: Response recommends introducing Failure type or UseCase base interfaces as one of the first steps

assertions.name: incremental-per-feature-mentioned
assertions.criteria: Response mentions migrating one feature at a time without breaking other features

assertions.name: order-compatible-with-10-steps
assertions.criteria: The suggested migration order is compatible with the canonical 10-step incremental refactoring order (domain models before repositories, repositories before replacing BLoC direct calls)
